raw_response:
Another year, another season. I'm 50 now, been farming these fields since I was 20. My mother-in-law taught me, and I've learned by watching my own land year after year. I don't read books, but I remember every harvest — which years the wheat turned yellow too early, which years the maize grew tall and thick.

I've got my 8 mu, same as always. Wheat in winter, maize in summer. My son works over in Handan at a factory, sends some money home now and then, but I don't like to count on it. My husband is here, and my daughter-in-law helps when the children are at school. We do most of the work ourselves. I don't hire people unless we're really stuck for time.

**For the wheat:** I'll plant around October 10th, same as the whole village. I buy improved seed — not the most expensive kind, but the one that's done well for me the past few years. Costs me about 50 yuan per mu. When I plant, I spread almost a full bag of that compound fertilizer on each mu — the shop sells it in big bags, and one bag is about right for two mu, so I use half a bag per mu. That's my base. Then come spring, when the wheat is jointing and looks a bit yellow, I'll walk the field with a bucket of urea and scatter some by hand. Maybe about 15 kg per mu. I irrigate three times: once before winter so the seedlings don't freeze, once at jointing when it needs to grow fast, and once when the grain is filling. Pumping water costs money, so three times is enough. I spray herbicide in early spring, and if I see aphids like last year, I'll spray insecticide too. I expect about 400 kg per mu if the weather doesn't do anything strange.

**For the maize:** The wheat comes off around June 10th, and I have to get the maize in quick — sometimes only a few days before the soil dries too much. I hire the tractor from the village with that no-till planter. Costs a bit, but it's fast, and time is everything. I buy hybrid seed every year — can't save it, everyone knows that — about 60 yuan per mu. I put compound fertilizer in the row at planting, a bit less than for wheat, about 40 kg per mu. Then when the maize is knee-high, I topdress with urea, maybe 10 kg per mu. I irrigate twice if the rains don't come — July and August can turn dry. One spray for weeds, and I watch for corn borer. My cousin's farm had bad borers two years ago, so I'm careful. I hope for 450 kg per mu.

I don't spend more than I have to. My neighbor Old Wang puts on more fertilizer than me, but his son has a good job and he can afford it. I stick to what works. Better to have a bit of cash in my pocket than to pour everything into the field and pray for good prices.
